SchoolRecord.title: SchoolRecord
SchoolRecord.description: Authoritative source record held by the School issuer, and the ONLY source of a SchoolCertificate's claims. oid4vc-school resolves the AUTHENTICATED national id to exactly one record here; neither a wallet nor a caller may supply or select learnerId or schoolStudentId (REQUIREMENTS §1.4). The College and University issuers must not read it.

schoolStudentId.title: School student ID
schoolStudentId.description: The School's own identifier, e.g. SCH-2019-0837. Issuer-side only: never a credential claim, so neither verifier learns which school roll a learner sat on.

learnerId.title: Learner ID
learnerId.description: The Education correlation identifier, e.g. EDU-L-004512. This is the value both verifiers correlate across the three credentials. A different namespace and sequence from nationalId and from every institution's student id, because PRODUCT forbids treating any of them as interchangeable.

nationalId.title: National ID
nationalId.description: Issuer-side lookup only, e.g. NAT-70011234. Matched against the authenticated Keycloak account's nationalId claim to decide whose credential may be issued. NEVER issued as a credential claim and never disclosed to either verifier (REQUIREMENTS §2, §7).

completionStatus.title: Completion status
completionStatus.description: Controlled vocabulary. Only COMPLETED satisfies either policy; the others exist so that a genuine, fully verified credential can still produce NOT ELIGIBLE.

completionYear.title: Completion year
completionYear.description: Year of completion. Disclosable, and requested by both verifiers so a demo can show the sequence is plausible, but never used as an eligibility threshold in this iteration.

percentage.title: Percentage
percentage.description: Percentage, 0 through 100, at most two decimal places. Compared against a threshold with integer arithmetic (services/verifier/src/domains/education/percentage.mjs) so that a boundary is exact: 60 must pass a >=60 rule and 59.99 must not, regardless of how the value survives JSON. A value with finer precision than the schema permits is a MALFORMED claim, not a business answer. The Master's rule requires >=60 here; the job rule does not use it at all, which is what makes the two policies visibly different over one credential.
